days.label: Monday
days.text: Monday itself is on the quiet side, and the anchor is Kaleo ($49) at Higher Ground Ballroom in South Burlington at 8, with Vincent Lima opening. Doors open at 7 , and the Icelandic band is out behind the ten year anniversary of A/B, the record that gave us "Way Down We Go." Baseball people get the cheapest night out in town at Hot Dog Hysteria Night at Centennial Field, first pitch 6:35, where the whole hook is 25 cent hot dogs, so come hungry and get there early. Runners can meet at Skirack's Run Club on Main Street, which gathers at 5:45 in the shop's Run Center. Readers have the Book Club For Curious Women [MEETUP] at 6:30 in Essex Junction, which works through a couple chapters at a time rather than a whole book, under what the host cheerfully calls Vegas rules. Quiz types can settle in for Trivia with Craig Mitchell at the Monkey House in Winooski at 7. If you want something you can wander into any day this week, Color & Scale is up through September at the BCA Center, Leah Barranco's vivid paintings of the creatures living in Vermont's waterways. And at 2 in the afternoon South Burlington breaks ground on the Walk Bike Bridge near Staples, the crossing that will finally let people walk and bike over I-89 away from the Exit 14 ramps, with an opening penciled in for late 2028.

days.label: Tuesday
days.text: Tuesday fills up fast. Shelburne Farms hosts a Pasture Walk & Picnic from 3 to 5:30, a guided mile or two through the pastures looking at soil, grazing and what all of it does for the land, closing with a spread of farm raised food, free with preregistration. Cyclists have two very different options, the no drop EZ Breezy Bike Ride rolling out of Local Motion on Steele Street at 6 with music and volunteers keeping everyone together, or the Tuesday trail running series at Catamount ($20 online, $25 day of) in Williston at 6, which is a timed race rather than a social jog. Singers should know that the Green Mountain Chorus guest night at Grace United Methodist in Essex Junction from 7 to 8 is open to anybody curious about barbershop harmony, men and women both, and they are working up Beatles material. Readers can join the Charity & Sylvia discussion at the Winooski Memorial Library from 6 to 7:30 for this year's Vermont Reads pick, with free copies still sitting at the library, or spend the same window at Board Games for Adults at the Essex Free Library, refreshments included. The Lake Monsters run Youth Sports Night at 6:35 with a pregame parade and a postgame catch out in the outfield. Eat at American Flatbread on St. Paul Street anytime from 4 to 10 and Vermont Parks Forever collects $3.50 from every large pie. Early risers can bring opinions about the city's next twenty five years to the PlanBTV 2050 coffee hour at Schmanska Park from 10 to 11, coffee and pastries on them, though they do want an RSVP by email first.

days.label: Wednesday
days.text: Wednesday is the fullest day of the four even with rain in the forecast. Our own Pick-up Basketball [MEETUP] runs 5:30 to 7:30 at Pomeroy Park in the Old North End, outdoors and free like always. Come play, come hang, either is welcome. Colchester has the biggest draw of the week with the Phil Abair Band at Sam Mazza's Farm Market from 6 to 8, lawn chairs and blankets on the grass, picnics welcome, food and a licensed beverage cart on site. Horror readers should not sleep on Paul Tremblay at The SuperStore in Williston from 6 to 9, the New York Times bestselling novelist launching Dead but Dreaming of Electric Sheep, free with registration. Cyclists get the 9 mile ride from Switchback [MEETUP] at 5:30, a flat out and back up the path to Leddy and home inside 45 minutes, after which everyone regroups at the taproom for Buns & Brew night. Speaking of Leddy, Beach Bites takes over the park from 5 to 8 with food trucks, lawn games, live music and free public skating in the arena, and this is the last regularly scheduled one of the summer. Downtown, Passeggiata gets the bricks strolling at 6 in the Italian evening tradition, and Summer Sketchbook Club gathers at Daydream Art Supply on Church Street from 5. Shelburne Vineyard runs its Wednesday Wine Down market from 5 to 9, Doma Bar hosts the weekly All-Inclusive Dyke-Tacular from 5 to 10, and dancers can drop into open West Coast Swing practice on Crowley Street at 6:45. The Craftsbury Chamber Players ($25) play Elley-Long in Colchester at 7:30 in their 60th season, with an artist chat at 6:45 and free admission for kids 12 and under. Cooks can bring a dish to Vegan in Vermont at Fletcher Free from 6 to 8, though that registration has to happen in person at the library. Anyone curious how collective giving works can sit in on 100+ Women Who Care at the University Mall from 5 to 6:30.

days.label: Thursday
days.text: Thursday is the marquee. Thundercat ($54.50, kids 12 and under free) plays Waterfront Park at 7, and the Grammy winning bassist wraps a crowd up in jazz fusion, funk and soul like nobody else working. Already scored my ticket so I’ll see you down there! Doors are at 6 with Maari of 99 Neighbors opening, the show runs rain or shine, and blankets and chairs are welcome though outside food and drink are not. Our group's Trivia at Four Quarters [MEETUP] starts at 6 in Winooski, and if you can get there a little early please help us grab a table. South Burlington throws SB Nite Out at Veterans Memorial Park from 5:30 to 8 with food trucks, the band Quadra, and a Cirque de Fuego fire performance, while Colchester counters with a free summer concert at Lower Bayside Park at 6:30, where InCahoots covers everything from Charlie Daniels to AC/DC. Church Street runs Party on the Bricks from 5:30 to 8 with Barbacoa playing outside Gaku Ramen, and Williston gets Crystal Ship doing the Doors at Maple Tree Place in Williston from 6 to 8, free.

days.label: Thursday
days.text: Thursday also has plenty for people who would rather do something than watch something. The Old East End holds its monthly Potluck in the Park at Schmanska Park from 5:30 to 8, and you genuinely do not need to RSVP or bring a dish to show up, eat, and meet a neighbor. Women's Pickup Flag Football kicks off at 6 on the UVM rugby pitch, seven on seven, free, open to women and LGBTQIA+ players at any ability level. Methods & Means at Generator puts five working makers in a circle of chairs from 6 to 8 to talk honestly about how creative people actually pay the bills, with the floor open for questions. Colchester's Burnham library runs a free adults only dinosaur escape room at 4, though spots are tight enough that you can only sign up yourself and one friend. Artists can join the drop in Thursday figure drawing ($15-20 suggested) at the Odd Fellows hall on North Avenue from 7 to 9, eighteen and up with ID at the door. Early birds can meet the BTV Cleanup Crew in front of Kru at the top of Church Street at 7:30 in the morning, where gloves and bags are provided and nobody minds if you peel off when work calls. Comedy fans get former SNL writer Rosebud Baker ($25) opening a three night run at Vermont Comedy Club at 7. Networkers have Internpalooza at Hula from 5, a storytelling showcase and pitch competition with appetizers and drinks. The Solarpunk Book Club meets at the Peace & Justice Center at 5:30, and the Lake Monsters close out the homestand at 6:35 by handing the first 500 fans a Champ toothbrush holder bobblehead .
